subject: Mutual plan: success KPIs, gated acceptance, and test matrix for Mediflow eval
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Allen Curtis <allen@mediflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft mutual plan: KPIs, gated acceptance, and test matrix for the eval

Allen — thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, I put together an initial mutual plan draft that ties the evaluation timeline to concrete success indicators and handoff gates so both teams are aligned before we start integration work. Attached are: 1) a one-page MAP draft and 2) a suggested evaluation test matrix.

High-level ask: please review the success KPIs below and flag any items that are blockers for procurement or security. If these look good, can we lock the timeline on Friday (Feb 13) so Redwood can schedule a reserved test pool?

Proposed success KPIs (must pass to progress to pilot):
- Avg latency (95th percentile) for typical query: <= 220ms across 1k samples
- First-token latency for streaming chat: <= 120ms median
- End-to-end throughput: sustain 5 concurrent sessions with <10% queueing
- Relevance concordance: automated score >= 0.88 on provided golden set (50 prompts)
- Safety/regression: zero critical hallucination incidents in smoke tests; logged incidents < 2

Gated acceptance flow (3 gates):
Gate A — Trial readiness (API integration & auth): basic integration done, shared test keys validated, and SOC2 evidence reviewed.
Gate B — Performance & quality (runbook-driven): automated load & concordance checks pass on our test harness with samples agreed in the matrix.
Gate C — Go/no-go to pilot (operational): monitoring hooks enabled, rollback plan agreed, and billing/commit terms confirmed.

Acceptance tests (short):
- Integration smoke: sample prompts + intentional edge cases to verify schema preservation and tool calling behavior.
- Load test: 30-minute ramp to target concurrency with KV cache warmed, measuring token SLOs.
- Concordance check: run golden set through candidate model config; generate concordance report and human spot-check 10% of failures.

Next steps: I recommend a 30-min call on Thu 11th to walk through the matrix and finalize any procurement asks. If you prefer, Marissa will own the runbook details and schedule the test window.

Attachments: 20260210_MAP_draft_v1.pdf (MAP summary), mediflow-eval-test-matrix.xlsx (test cases + owner columns)

—
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Rafael — thanks for the clear draft and the headset demo. Quick notes from my side after an internal sync with Engineering and Procurement:

Engineering feedback:
- Latency targets look reasonable; we want to add an alternate SLA for 99th percentile for our higher-variance queries (target <= 600ms).
- For concordance, can we expand the golden set to 75 prompts; we'll share 25 additional edge-case prompts focused on clinical abbreviations.

Procurement request:
- We need a short appendix that defines data retention during the eval and the customer-controlled key flow (KMS). Procurement copied.

Timing: Thu the 12th works for a 30-min walkthrough; prefer early afternoon (13:00 PT). If the Thursday call finalizes the matrix, we can sign the MAP and target test window Feb 17–19.

Also: please confirm what evidence you can provide for SOC2 items around logging and access reviews — that will speed procurement.

Allen
Allen Curtis, Head of Platform Engineering
Mediflow Inc.

- Feb 19: joint decision meeting to confirm pilot go/no-go and sign-off

If that looks good to you, I'll push the updated MAP to the Drive after the call and attach the SOC2 summary. Rafael — after the meeting please create the hubspot deal record with timeline so procurement has the paperwork.

Thanks — see you at 13.
